correctness.rationale: For 0<p<1 every length-three word occurs with finite moments. The first-absorption conditional-moment derivation gives exact rational covariances, independently confirmed by a two-flag Markov reward system for all sixteen complement orbits symbolically. All normalized denominators have strictly positive analytic factors; exact Sturm counts and gcd proofs certify interior zeros and simplicity. The package verification returns 16 symbolic checks, 84 rational checks and 16 root-count certificates. Neither simulation nor truncation proves the infinite sample-path assertions.

Fu–Chang (2002) describes a generating-function method for compound-pattern waiting times, not a pairwise parameter-bias phase diagram.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader exact-PGF methods are acknowledged. A general algorithm determining a joint distribution can in principle compute any mixed moment; the explicit enumeration of all sign regimes and proof of at most two sign changes for this natural family are not stated in the inspected sources. This is the key residual priority vulnerability, not concealed by terminological differences.

value.rationale: Length-three binary words form a canonical complete Penney-game comparison class. The pair covariance dependence can reverse twice as the coin bias varies, a phenomenon not inferred from first-hitting means or winning probabilities. A complete 28-pair sign taxonomy (7 universally positive, 3 universally negative, 14 with one crossover, 4 with two) and algebraic transition points provide a naturally motivated, sharp structural classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
